description: Apply the backend correctness and security fixes identified in the audit. These are server-side TypeScript changes in server/. All changes must keep `npm run lint` and `npm run build` green. Do not change external behavior beyond the fixes described. This feature is independent of FEAT-003 (frontend) except that both must build cleanly.
steps: Fix invalid AI model default: in server/agents.ts line ~99, change the default from 'gemini-3.6-flash' to 'gemini-2.0-flash' so it matches every other module (server/calling-agent.ts, server/letter-generator.ts, server/whatsapp-bot.ts, server/whatsapp-webhook.ts, server/content-safety.ts all use gemini-2.0-flash). This restores the AI chat when GEMINI_MODEL is unset.

Replace insecure randomness for security tokens with crypto-secure generation. node:crypto is already imported in server/auth.ts (randomBytes is available). Add or reuse a helper like `function secureSixDigitCode(): string { return (randomInt(0, 1_000_000)).toString().padStart(6, '0'); }` using `randomInt` from node:crypto, and use it at server/auth.ts:756 (registration email OTP), server/auth.ts:1049 (AI PIN), and server/auth.ts:1557 (the third OTP code). In server/sms-otp.ts line ~13, replace `Math.floor(100000 + Math.random() * 900000)` with the same crypto-secure approach (import randomInt from node:crypto). Preserve the exact 6-digit zero-padded format and all surrounding logic. Do NOT change the deriveOtpCode HMAC-based login OTP (that path is already deterministic-by-design and secure).

Add missing HTTP security headers in server/security.ts configureSecurity(). In the existing response-header middleware (where X-Content-Type-Options etc. are set), also set: `res.setHeader('X-Frame-Options', 'DENY')`; a Content-Security-Policy that ALLOWS the resources the app actually uses (script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com https://cdn.jsdelivr.net; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com https://cdn.jsdelivr.net; img-src 'self' data: https:; connect-src 'self'; frame-src https://maps.google.com https://www.google.com https://maps.googleapis.com; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none') - verify against index.html (Google Fonts + jsdelivr geist font) and src/pages/ContactPage.tsx (Google Maps iframe) so nothing is broken; include 'unsafe-inline' for style-src because Tailwind/motion inject inline styles and React sets style attributes. Only send Strict-Transport-Security when secure (production/Vercel): `if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' || process.env.VERCEL) res.setHeader('Strict-Transport-Security', 'max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains')`. Keep Vite dev server working: in development the CSP must still allow the Vite client (it uses inline scripts and websocket) - if a strict script-src 'self' would break `npm run dev`, gate the CSP so it is only enforced in production, or add the minimal dev allowances. Prefer: enforce full CSP only when NODE_ENV==='production', and in dev either omit CSP or use a report-only/relaxed variant. Document the choice in a code comment.

Fix phoneVerified inconsistency: in server/auth.ts the /api/otp/verify success response (around line 331 area, the res.json user object) should include `phoneVerified: user.phone_verified ?? false` to match the /api/auth/login response (around line 457) so the client receives consistent user shape after either login path. Load phone_verified where needed (loadActiveUser already selects phone_verified).
Run `npm run lint` (tsc --noEmit) and fix any type errors introduced. Run `npm run build` and confirm both the vite build and the esbuild server bundle succeed.
Record what changed and any decisions (especially the CSP dev-vs-prod handling) in this feature's findings field.
acceptance_criteria: No `Math.random()` remains for generating OTP codes or the AI PIN in server/auth.ts and server/sms-otp.ts; they use node:crypto (randomInt or randomBytes). The output is still a zero-padded 6-digit string.

server/security.ts sets X-Frame-Options, a Content-Security-Policy, and (in production) Strict-Transport-Security, without breaking Google Fonts, the jsdelivr geist font, the Google Maps iframe, or the Vite dev server.
The /api/otp/verify success response includes phoneVerified, matching /api/auth/login.
`npm run lint` exits 0 and `npm run build` succeeds.
verification: Run `npm run lint` and confirm exit 0.
Run `npm run build` and confirm vite build + esbuild bundle both succeed.
Grep to confirm no Math.random remains in the OTP/PIN generation lines of server/auth.ts and server/sms-otp.ts, and that agents.ts uses gemini-2.0-flash.
findings: All four backend fixes applied and verified. (1) server/agents.ts callGemini default model changed from 'gemini-3.6-flash' to 'gemini-2.0-flash' (line 99), matching the other server modules. (2) Added a shared helper secureSixDigitCode() in server/auth.ts (before loadActiveUser) using randomInt from node:crypto (imported alongside the existing crypto imports); used it at the registration email OTP, AI PIN, and forgot-password OTP sites (previously lines 756/1049/1557, now shifted by the helper insertion). server/sms-otp.ts generateOtp() now imports randomInt and returns randomInt(0, 1_000_000).toString().padStart(6, '0'). Output remains a zero-padded 6-digit string. The HMAC-based deriveOtpCode login OTP was intentionally left untouched. Note: server/calling-agent.ts still uses Math.random for a non-security call reference ID (VC-...) which is out of scope for this feature. (3) server/security.ts configureSecurity now sets X-Frame-Options: DENY unconditionally, and a full Content-Security-Policy plus Strict-Transport-Security ONLY when NODE_ENV==='production' || VERCEL. CSP dev-vs-prod decision: a strict script-src 'self' breaks the Vite dev server (inline scripts + HMR websocket), so the CSP is omitted entirely in development and enforced only in production; documented via a code comment. The production CSP allows Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com CSS, fonts.gstatic.com files), the jsdelivr Geist font (cdn.jsdelivr.net), the Google Maps iframe (maps.google.com/www.google.com/maps.googleapis.com in frame-src), and uses 'unsafe-inline' for style-src for Tailwind/motion/React inline styles. Verified index.html and src/pages/ContactPage.tsx external resource usage matches the policy. (4) /api/otp/verify success response now includes phoneVerified: user.phone_verified ?? false, matching /api/auth/login; loadActiveUser already selects phone_verified. Verification: `npm run lint` (tsc --noEmit) exits 0 and `npm run build` (vite + esbuild) succeeds. The vite 671kB chunk-size warning is pre-existing and belongs to the frontend feature (FEAT-003), not this one.
